title: Perception for Smart Bike Lights: Real-Time Embedded Bike Headlight Control Using a Single-Model Convolutional Neural Network
pdfName: Perception for Smart Bike Lights — Full report
author: Sagnik Das, Muhid Abid Siddiqui and Nitish Devrani
lead: A lightweight CNN for real-time bicycle headlight control on a Raspberry Pi.
about: This report presents a vision-based adaptive bicycle headlight that predicts off, dim or high beam from a forward-facing camera stream. A lightweight residual CNN combines illumination and vehicle-proximity cues, using policy-derived BDD100K labels for training and a Raspberry Pi for GPIO-driven headlight control. The reported 93.99% classification accuracy measures agreement with the derived labeling policy, rather than real-world glare safety.

title: Cloud Economics: Cloud Specs (A WebApp with RAG-Powered Chatbot)
pdfName: Cloud Economics: Cloud Specs — Full report
author: Nitish Devrani
lead: A multi-cloud advisory platform for comparing compute instances, answering pricing questions and building infrastructure bundles.
about: This report describes Cloud Specs, a React-based platform for comparing AWS, Azure and GCP compute instances. It combines a filtered, weighted recommendation engine with a RAG-powered pricing assistant and a conversational infrastructure shopping agent. The retrieval pipeline uses the Arcana vector-database service and Qwen embeddings, while language models hosted on Academic Cloud support the assistant. The report focuses on the interactive platform and its use of collected cloud-pricing data.

title: How Far Can You Compress CLIP? A Systematic Study of Pruning and Quantization for Edge Deployment
author: Nitish Devrani
lead: A systematic study of pruning, quantization and their ordering in CLIP-family models.
about: The full course project paper reports 300+ experiments across CLIP ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16 and MobileCLIP-S1, comparing zero-shot accuracy under pruning and quantization. It includes sparsity sweeps, three-seed variance analysis and ImageNette validation, with explicit distinctions between simulated low-bit quantization, realistic storage estimates and actual edge deployment.

title: A Memory-Augmented LLM Agent for Open-Ended Navigation in MiniGrid
author: Vegim Bytyqi, Nitish Devrani and Pawan Saxena
lead: Grounding an LLM navigation policy in persistent spatial memory, a local symbolic map and structured prompts.
about: A February 2026 paper on a memory-augmented gpt-4.1-mini agent for BabyAI/MiniGrid. The architecture combines textual observation encoding, persistent spatial memory, a local symbolic map, subgoal prompting and action validation. Sample runs illustrate successful navigation and object interaction alongside residual policy looping and episode-to-episode variance.

title: Bias in AI: On Cultural Bias in Large Language Models
author: Nitish Devrani, Omar Nabail and Amr Reyad
lead: A small-scale study of culturally grounded LLM responses and the agreement between automated judges and human annotators.
about: Using 30 culturally grounded cloze-style prompts and 330 response items, this study examines Arabic cultural context across ChatGPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet-4.5, Qwen3-Max, DeepSeek-V3.2 and Gemini-3. The prompt set draws on CAMeL examples translated into English and additional prompts. Access conditions include Germany versus a U.S. VPN, plus ChatGPT pro and non-pro accounts. Five blinded LLM judges assign bias labels by majority vote, with a human sanity check involving nine Arabic-culture-knowledgeable annotators on responses to eight prompts. Observed bias rates range from 6.7% to 30.0%. Individual agreement is low among both human annotators (Fleiss’ κ = 0.117) and LLM judges (κ = 0.112), while human-majority and LLM-majority labels agree on 82.3% of the 62 overlapping items (Cohen’s κ = 0.592). Account-tier, location and exploratory between-model comparisons were not statistically significant in this small sample. The findings highlight culturally mismatched completions and the subjectivity of bias labeling, rather than establishing a reliable model ranking.

title: A Perfectly Frictionless Companion Is a Perfectly Stunted One: On Sycophantic AI and the Eclipse of Moral Selfhood
author: Nitish Devrani
lead: A philosophical examination of AI companionship, moral autonomy and the difference between satisfaction and human flourishing.
about: This essay examines a hypothetical AI companion designed to affirm every opinion and remove disagreement from the user’s relationships. Its Developmental Deprivation Argument holds that moral growth requires challenge, while a fully sycophantic companion removes those conditions. Drawing on Aristotelian virtue ethics, Kantian autonomy and liberal perfectionism, the essay argues that persistent affirmation can undermine practical wisdom and moral selfhood. It considers a consequentialist defence grounded in wellbeing and freely chosen companionship, then responds by questioning how the system shapes preferences and whether subjective satisfaction is sufficient for flourishing. A closing meta-ethical reflection defends a broadly realist position while acknowledging that its assumptions about autonomy, challenge and objective wellbeing remain open to scrutiny. This is a normative philosophical argument, rather than an empirical study of AI users.
